title: Atlas — microbenchmarks (legacy)
description: make microbenchmarks local — febft PBFT. Panels are generated against the metrics this suite actually emits; see the 'About this suite' note for what its metric level leaves out.

list.name: host
list.label: Node
list.description: Atlas tags every point with host=NodeId(n): replicas are 0..n-1, clients start at 1000. Keep multi/includeAll on — the values contain parentheses, and Grafana only regex-escapes multi-value variables.

list.name: run
list.label: Run
list.description: The `extra` tag: 'None' unless the run set INFLUX_EXTRA. Suites share one database and several measurement names, so filter by Run before comparing anything across protocols.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description:
Mean across replicas. Every replica handles every operation, so the mean is cluster throughput — a sum would multiply it by n.

This suite registers no executor metrics, so throughput is read off the ordering protocol instead.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") FROM "OPERATIONS_ORDERED" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(none)

panels.title: Client request rate
panels.description: Summed over client processes — each drives a disjoint slice of the load, so here the sum is the real total.

targets.query: SELECT sum("rate") FROM (SELECT mean("value") AS "rate" FROM "CLIENT_RQ_PER_SECOND" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host") GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(none)

panels.title: Client latency
panels.description: End-to-end at the client: send → f+1 matching replies.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") FROM "CLIENT_RQ_LATENCY" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(none)

options.content:
**make microbenchmarks local** — febft PBFT, replica metrics at `MetricLevel::Trace`, clients at `MetricLevel::Info`.

The pre-SMR-Core benchmark, kept for comparison against the older API. It registers neither atlas-smr-core nor atlas-smr-execution, so the request pre-processing and execution rows other suites rely on simply do not exist here — there is no CONSENSUS_WAIT_TIME and no OPERATIONS_EXECUTED_PER_SECOND. Throughput has to be read off the ordering protocol (OPERATIONS_ORDERED) and the clients.

Its replica runs at Trace, so what it does report, it reports in full.

---
**Registered but not emitted here** (3). This suite passes these crates' `metrics()` to `initialize_metrics`, but `with_metric_level(MetricLevel::Trace)` filters them out, so no panel below draws them — raise the level in the binary if you need one:

`CLIENT_RQ_SEND_TIME` (Trace), `RQ_BATCH_TRACKING` (Disabled), `RQ_CLIENT_TRACKING` (Disabled)

panels.title: PBFT — consensus phases
panels.description: The pre-prepare → prepare → commit ladder. The two →-transitions each contain a quorum-wide round trip, so under a WAN profile they are where the added latency lands; the phase latencies themselves stay local.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") FROM "PROPOSE_LATENCY" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") FROM "PRE_PREPARE_LATENCY" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") FROM "PRE_PREPARE_TO_PREPARE_LATENCY" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") FROM "PREPARE_LATENCY" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") FROM "PREPARE_TO_COMMIT_LATENCY" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") FROM "COMMIT_LATENCY" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)

panels.title: Ordering throughput and pre-prepare analysis
panels.description: OPERATIONS_ORDERED is the protocol's own throughput — compare it against the executor's OPERATIONS_EXECUTED_PER_SECOND: a persistent gap means execution is falling behind consensus.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") FROM "OPERATIONS_ORDERED" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") FROM "PRE_PREPARE_RQ_ANALYSIS" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") FROM "PRE_PREPARE_LOG_ANALYSIS" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)

panels.title: State installation
panels.description: Cost of catching a replica up after it fell behind or restarted.

panels.title: Client-observed behaviour
panels.description: What the load generator sees. The only view that is not the system marking its own homework — if these and the replica-side numbers disagree, believe these.

panels.title: Client request rate
panels.description: One series per client container (NodeId 1000+), each aggregating N_CLIENTS logical clients. Counter metrics are reset every collection, so a point is already a per-second rate.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") FROM "CLIENT_RQ_PER_SECOND" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)

panels.description: Ordered latency is send → f+1 matching replies. CLIENT_RQ_SEND_TIME is registered at Trace, so it only appears in suites whose client runs at that level.

panels.title: Host resources
panels.description: Written by the Atlas-Metrics OS thread every 250 ms. These bypass the metric registry and the level filter, so they are present in every suite.

panels.title: CPU per node
panels.description: Averaged over cores: OS_CPU_USER is written once per core (tag `cpu`) as a 0..1 fraction.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") FROM "OS_CPU_USER" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)

panels.title: Process RSS per node
panels.description: Resident memory of the Atlas process, not the whole host.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") FROM "OS_RAM_USAGE" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)

panels.title: Network per node
panels.description:
Bytes between 250 ms samples, scaled x4 to a per-second rate.

Caveat: os_mon.rs crosses the directions — OS_NETWORK_UP is summed from received() and OS_NETWORK_DOWN from transmitted(). Trust the series names.

targets.query: SELECT mean("value") * 4 FROM "OS_NETWORK_UP" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
SELECT mean("value") * 4 FROM "OS_NETWORK_DOWN" WHERE ("host" =~ /^$host$/ AND "extra" =~ /^$run$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(none)
